title: Blind adversarial review: decision-tree barrier (Theorem DT, Theorem P, Corollary P1)
question: Are Theorem DT (N <= 9*2^L - 1 for equality-branching trees), Lemma A, Theorem P and Corollary P1 (N <= 40*2^(2D+L)) of HYP-dbe79a50 correct as stated?
claims: Theorem DT: paper proof sound. Model (state per root path, free constants and tests, divisions only where executed), generic-path degree <= 2^t, deviating nodes <= 2^(L+1)-1 (only the <= L+1 registers of the generic path count, depth irrelevant) and final arithmetic N <= 3*2^L+2+3(2^(L+1)-1) = 9*2^L-1 all verified. Not Lean-checked.

Lemma A for arbitrary G is true but the author's proof is incomplete: forward-only propagation from one consecutive pair reaches x_(r-1), x_(r-2) but the closing contradiction needs A=B at x_1 and A=2B at x_2, which hold only if 1,2 in G. Repair: also propagate backward from the pair (identity at n, divide by B(x_n)B(x_(n+1)), coprimality gives B != 0) down to k=1,2. The Lean plan 'generalise base case of prop' is insufficient.

Theorem P is correct with corrections: exclude k=j (other conjugate is x(O)), 2j != 0 must hold in F, define A, R, j; nonvanishing also follows from Q -> -Q symmetry and evenness without irreducibility and for composite r.

Corollary P1 as stated in the HYP is INCORRECT: no characteristic hypothesis. Counterexample F=GF(3^7), y^2=x^3+x+b, a point of order 2188, N=1093 > 640 = 40*2^(2*2+0): partition by k mod 3 (3<=2^2 classes) with constant outputs (L=0). Correct with hypothesis char F = 0 or char F > N; constant 40 and exponent 2D+L then valid (derivation gives 11).

Empirical (finite toy evidence only): Lemma A search on toy curves never exceeded 3d centres (max found 2,3,5 for d=1,2,3); random trees L<=4: 0 violations of the deviation/generic-leaf claims; Theorem P polynomial degree<=4d, vanishing and nonvanishing held in 480 trials on prime and composite point orders.
next_action: Revise HYP-dbe79a50: add hypothesis char F > N (or 0) to Corollary P1, state the model explicitly, define A/R/j in Theorem P, repair Lemma A proof with backward propagation. Then formalize in Lean (tree datatype, generic path, bidirectional-propagation Lemma A, Theorem P) and obtain re-review of the revised statement.
notes: Reviewer model (self-reported, not verified by runtime metadata): Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). Author report read only after initial findings were written. No Lean build run; no files outside owned outputs edited. Scratch code in the session scratchpad dtreview/ directory.

review.rationale: Core mathematics of DT, Lemma A and Theorem P survives adversarial checking, but (1) Corollary P1 is false as stated (missing characteristic hypothesis, explicit counterexample) and (2) the proof of Lemma A for non-interval G has a gap (backward propagation missing) that also invalidates the stated Lean plan. Both are repairable without changing the headline bound.
counterexamples: Corollary P1 over GF(3^7): E y^2=x^3+x+b with a point of order 2188, N=1093 > 640 = 40*2^(2D+L), D=2 (classes k mod 3), L=0 (constant output k mod 3); every pair k,k+j in a class has 3|j so 2j=0 and Theorem P does not apply.
Lemma A, toy search on F_p (p 31..47), d=1..3: no violation of centres <= 3d (max 2d-1..2d). Random trees (p=101, L<=4): no violation of generic-path claims.
review.complexity: Counts only field operations (+,-,*,/) on a path; tests free. Bound N <= 9*2^L-1, i.e. L >= log2(N+1)-3.17; no bit-complexity, comparison, bit-extraction or Legendre-test claim. Experiments cost seconds each (stdlib Python).
review.limitations: Paper-level review, nothing Lean-checked in this run; toy-curve experiments are finite evidence not proof; generalized Lemma A repair and Theorem P function-field argument are my own derivations, not machine-verified; GF(3^7) counterexample is logical plus numeric group order, not a full program execution; model identity self-reported.
review.initial_packet: HYP-dbe79a50 statement (question/claims text) plus MathResearch/ECDLP/RationalSLP.lean; author report RUN-3386b45f withheld until initial findings were written.
